chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureyd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
From the Sunnah of the Sent Prophets is the cleaning oneself after relieving oneself, and circumcision.

key_terms.الاسْتِنْجَاءُ: Cleansing the private parts after relieving oneself, a key act of ritual purity.
key_terms.السُّنَنِ: Traditions or practices of the Prophet.
key_terms.الْمُرْسَلِينَ: The Sent Prophets, referring to those sent with divine messages.

ai.seo_question: What are the Sunnah practices of the Prophets regarding ritual purity and circumcision?
ai.summary: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) identifies istinja' and khitan as fundamental 'sunnahs of the sent ones,' linking physical hygiene directly to the prophetic legacy. In Shia jurisprudence, this elevates these acts from mere customs to essential components of ritual purity (taharah), reflecting the holistic nature of the Prophets' way of life. This narration underscores the continuity between the physical and spiritual dimensions of worship in the Imami tradition.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Qasim Bin Bureyd, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas is the cleaning oneself after the toilet, and the circumcision’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Qasim ibn Burayd from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Of the Sunnah of prophets is draining al-Istinja’ (one’s urine) and circumcision.’”
